messages:
Alex: FYI I'm seeing steady-state churn in the continuous-batching scheduler: slots flip owners every ~2s which causes KV cache thrash and lots of tiny evictions. anyone else notice this?
Maria: yep, canary showed latency blips during lease flips.
Cheng: is this due to the short lease TTL + synchronous reclaim path?
Alex: seems so. current defaults: lease_ttl 2s, heartbeat 700ms. pattern: missed heartbeat -> immediate reclaim -> enqueue by new owner -> eviction of KV entries.
Sam: quick options: increase TTL, add jitter, or make reclaim lazy.
Maria: lazy reclaim seems promising: if a tenant had recent activity we avoid immediate reclaim for a few seconds to absorb microbursts.
Cheng: downside is reduced capacity if a node really dies. maybe exponential backoff on reclaim attempts rather than fixed TTL.
Alex: propose two reclaim modes: fast for confirmed failures, and slow for ambiguous misses.
Sam: if we lengthen TTL add a fastpath to evacuate latency-critical tenants to dedicated fastpool during a suspected node freeze.
Maria: KV warmup cost is critical. Each reclaim creates cold KV state; even a single cold miss increases tail latency.
Cheng: idea: grace token handshake. new owner probes previous owner; if previous owner answers within X ms it hands over a cache pointer. avoids full warmup.
Alex: handshake sketch: new owner issues a lease_probe to old owner; if it replies within 250ms transfer a cache pointer, otherwise full reclaim.
Sam: need to rate-limit probes to avoid storm during rebalances. cap probes per node per second.
Maria: add metrics: lease_state{tenant,slot,state,owner} and histogram reclaim_latency_ms. helps correlate reclaims with tail latency.
Cheng: admission control idea: if reclaim forces drops, track missed admission tokens and apply short-term throttle for that tenant to smooth load.
Alex: config prototype: lease_ttl_ms=5000, heartbeat_ms=800, reclaim_mode=two_phase, grace_window_ms=300, probe_timeout_ms=250, max_probes_per_sec=5.
Sam: in local tests TTL=5s reduced churn but a frozen node caused ~10% capacity loss; SLO implications need docing.
Maria: mitigate with kernel watchdog + controller-driven UNAVAILABLE marking to quickly detect frozen nodes.
Cheng: partial reclaim: instead of taking all slots on a miss, reclaim a fraction (eg 20%) immediately and the rest after grace to avoid cascading cold starts.
Alex: agree. fractional reclaim keeps tail down while restoring capacity.
Sam: make policies configurable per pool: hosted vs dedicated have different tolerances.
Maria: expose reclaim_policy per-pool: conservative|balanced|aggressive. default conservative for hosted.
Cheng: testing plan: 24h chaos run with pauses, node hiccups, verify metrics: reclaim_events/sec, kv_miss_rate, tenant_tail_latency.
Alex: actions: Maria -> dashboards and alert for reclaim_rate > 10/min sustained, Cheng -> prototype grace_token probe logic, Sam -> canary with lease_ttl_ms=5000 + fractional reclaim, Alex -> write RFC follow-up with SLO tradeoffs and the policy matrix.
infra-bot: canary deploy started for batch-scheduler lease-reconcile experiment (sha abc123)
Maria: also consider size-aware reclaim: small KV tenants can be aggressive, large KV tenants conservative.
Sam: policy matrix should consider {kv_size, tenant_sla, recent_activity}.
Alex: will capture all of this in the RFC. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
